transfer_note: A new standalone evaluation task. It carves nothing out of gpu02-eval-assist-20261001, so no registry transfer is required.
question: Are handover_block and place_object_basket achievable at all? All three of our arms score exactly zero on both (0/15 and 0/12 across 3 variants x 3 seeds).
why_torch: Shenlong GPU5 is held by another user (xzeng28). The official checkpoint and RoboTwin assets are public, so this task needs no private asset delivery - the blocker that stalled gpu02-eval-assist-20261001.

scenes.pairing: Exactly the seeds used by rae-policy-20261001, so results pair cell-by-cell with our 126 valid cells. Do not substitute the 20 fresh scenes proposed in baseline-official/protocol.json.
scenes.delivery: undecided - awaiting user decision between committing to this branch, private transfer, or Torch-side regeneration from seeds

render_divergence_measurement.why: Shenlong finds the scene physics reproduces to 1e-6 (proprio and every object pose assertion passes) while the render of that identical state diverges from the recorded reference by 0.52-1.03 uint8 levels across all 135 cells.
render_divergence_measurement.properties: Deterministic (spread 0.00 across 9 independent runs), localized, signed mean about zero so not an exposure or gamma shift.
render_divergence_measurement.current_gate: MAE > 1.0 is recorded as a technical failure; place_object_basket seed-1102008 sits at 1.0315 and was dropped from all 9 arms.
render_divergence_measurement.torch_value: Torch is a third rendering environment. A matching distribution implicates the collection/eval config difference (eval_mode, is_test, render_freq, save_data); a different one implicates a machine-dependent component.
render_divergence_measurement.instruction: Record initial_render_mae for every scene. If seed-1102008 also exceeds 1.0 on Torch, record the rejection honestly rather than widening the gate.

shenlong_side.retained_phase: vae48_native control arm (phase 2), to run on GPU5 once free
shenlong_side.phase2_purpose: Our study has no VAE arm at all - both raw768 and svae48 are DINOv3-based - so the RAE substitution has never actually been tested against the baseline it claims to beat.

prerequisites: Real GPU allocation reported (Slurm job id, model, UUID, available window); sbatch --test-only forecasts do not count
Time-boxed single-GPU preflight on training scenes only, no scoring scenes
failure_policy: Technical failures recorded separately, never counted as policy failures, no automatic retries.
